larthi.describe: A young woman in her mid twenties, low and quiet alto voice, dry, clipped and watchful, speaks little and evenly, never raises her voice except in danger; neutral unplaceable accent.

hasti.describe: A woman in her early thirties, warm, unhurried mezzo voice, kind and reassuring, puts strangers at ease, measured pace; neutral accent.

sethre.describe: A man around thirty, calm patient baritone, softly amused and wry, relaxed even pace; neutral accent.

arruns.describe: A big older man around sixty, deep, calm bass voice, slow and economical, says as little as he can, grounded and heavy.

popovic.describe: A city councillor in his early sixties, dry, precise, slightly nasal official voice, clipped consonants, used to being obeyed; faint Central European colouring.

arthur.describe: A door guard around forty, warm working-class baritone, plain and friendly, a little tired at the end of a shift; soft city accent.

lukac.describe: A chauffeur in his forties, laconic, wry low voice, unimpressed and a bit weary, faint Central European colouring.

inez.describe: A young waitress in her mid twenties, bright quick voice, nervous and defensive, words tumbling out, warm underneath.

milena.describe: A woman in her late thirties, dry teasing alto, fond and knowing, unhurried, gently mocking a friend.

police.describe: A uniformed police officer in his thirties, loud commanding parade-ground voice, sharp and authoritative.

rival.describe: A rough hard man in his thirties, gravelly urgent voice, a gang heavy shouting orders.

watcher.describe: A security desk man in his fifties, flat bureaucratic voice turned urgent, reporting over a telephone.

note: No voice is a clone of anyone. Fish has eight stock voices, so its men double: Adrian plays Arruns and Popovic, Jordan plays Arthur, Lukac and the rival, Ethan plays Sethre, the officer and the watcher.
